title: The whole gospel in a prayer (CCC 2761)
word: The whole gospel in a prayer
hookLine: Tertullian called the Our Father a summary of the whole gospel

lines: A FAITH ON AN INDEX CARD?
THE WEEK ARRIVES AT ONE PRAYER.
cards: Could a whole faith fit on an index card? An early Christian writer named Tertullian thought one already did.
In a work on prayer, he made a bold claim about the prayer Jesus taught, the Our Father, which you first met on day eleven: in it is a summary of the whole gospel. Not a piece of it. The whole.

The Catechism opens one of its articles on the Lord's Prayer with his words. All week it has walked around prayer: its springs, its way, its guides, its expressions, its battles, and Jesus's own prayer.
Now it opens the prayer itself. Today: the whole gospel in a prayer.

teach.h: A SHORT SUMMARY OF THE WHOLE GOSPEL.
teach.b: Tertullian's Latin is breviarium totius evangelii: a short summary of the whole gospel.
Test the claim against the prayer, in Matthew, in the Douay-Rheims: "Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven."
Then bread, forgiveness, temptation, and deliverance from evil. Now hold the Gospels next to it. Jesus begins preaching, in Matthew, with "the kingdom of heaven is at hand."
There's the second line. He feeds crowds with a few loaves: the bread. He forgives sinners and tells of a father running to meet a lost son: the forgiveness.
He's tempted in the desert, and frees people from evil spirits: the last lines. The prayer runs through the Gospel like a spine. The Catechism adds a practical thought from Tertullian.
Jesus also said ask and you shall receive, and everyone has needs of their own.
So this prayer comes first, as the foundation, and the rest of our asking is built on it. A Catholic praying for a sick friend isn't setting the Our Father aside; it goes underneath.
And it's short enough for a child to learn by heart, said at Mass, at a bedside, in a rosary, under the breath at a red light.
Small enough to carry anywhere. Big enough, Tertullian said, to hold everything.

how: Catholics pray the Our Father at every Mass, within the rosary and the Liturgy of the Hours, and in personal prayer; families teach it to children by heart.

games.q: what does “the whole gospel in a prayer” mean?
o: the Our Father as a summary of all Jesus taught
one book that collects all four Gospels
the Creed, said together at Sunday Mass

games.q: the whole gospel — tap the pairs.
p: called it a summary of the whole gospel
the kingdom of heaven is at hand
this prayer first, then our own asking

s: Tertullian called the Our Father a summary of only part of the gospel
his words: breviarium totius evangelii, a short summary of the whole gospel.
the Catechism opens an article on the Lord's Prayer by quoting Tertullian
its first paragraph quotes his claim.
Tertullian said the Our Father should replace all other asking
he said it comes first, as the foundation, and our own requests are built on it.

games.q: you have a sick friend and a hard week, and a long list of things to ask God for. in Tertullian's view, where does the Our Father fit?
o: say it instead of the list.
say it first, as the foundation.
games.why: Tertullian, quoted in the Catechism, says the Lord's Prayer comes first, as the foundation of further desires. the personal asking builds on it.

practice: Say the Our Father with one phrase on each out-breath, letting the pause between phrases be as long as the words: Our Father. Who art in heaven. Hallowed be thy name.
You may not reach the end, and that's fine; if you don't pray, simply listen to the phrases one at a time and notice which one catches.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole gospel. Short enough for a child, big enough for everything. Rest well.
